+package chi
+
+import (
+	"net/http"
+	"sort"
+	"strconv"
+	"strings"
+)
+
+// CORSOptions configures the Cross-Origin Resource Sharing headers written by
+// CORS, Mux.EnableCORS and Mux.EnableCORSWithOptions.
+type CORSOptions struct {
+	// AllowOrigin is the value of Access-Control-Allow-Origin. Use "*" to
+	// allow any origin. When it is empty the header is not written at all, so
+	// a zero CORSOptions grants nothing.
+	AllowOrigin string
+
+	// AllowMethods is the list written to Access-Control-Allow-Methods on a
+	// preflight response. When it is empty, the methods the router serves for
+	// the requested path are used instead, which is what lets a route be
+	// described by the methods registered on it.
+	AllowMethods []string
+
+	// AllowHeaders is the list written to Access-Control-Allow-Headers on a
+	// preflight response. When it is empty, the headers named by the
+	// preflight's Access-Control-Request-Headers are echoed back.
+	AllowHeaders []string
+
+	// ExposeHeaders is the list written to Access-Control-Expose-Headers,
+	// which names the response headers a browser may show to a script.
+	ExposeHeaders []string
+
+	// MaxAge is how many seconds a browser may cache a preflight response,
+	// written to Access-Control-Max-Age. Zero or less leaves the header out.
+	MaxAge int
+
+	// AllowCredentials writes Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true, which
+	// lets a browser send cookies and other credentials. A browser refuses a
+	// credentialed response whose origin is "*", so with AllowCredentials the
+	// request's own Origin is echoed back in place of the wildcard.
+	AllowCredentials bool
+}
+
+// DefaultCORSOptions returns the options that EnableCORS uses: any origin,
+// the request headers browsers and APIs most often need, a one hour
+// preflight cache and no fixed method list, so the router's own methods are
+// advertised.
+func DefaultCORSOptions() CORSOptions {
+	return CORSOptions{
+		AllowOrigin:  "*",
+		AllowHeaders: []string{"Accept", "Authorization", "Content-Type", "X-CSRF-Token"},
+		MaxAge:       3600,
+	}
+}
+
+// corsFallbackMethods is advertised on a preflight when neither the options
+// nor the router name any method, for example when CORS runs on a handler
+// that is not served by a chi Mux.
+var corsFallbackMethods = []string{
+	http.MethodGet, http.MethodHead, http.MethodPost, http.MethodPut,
+	http.MethodPatch, http.MethodDelete, http.MethodOptions,
+}
+
+// CORS returns a middleware that writes the CORS response headers described by
+// options and answers a preflight request itself with 204 No Content.
+//
+// A request is a preflight when it is an OPTIONS request that carries an
+// Access-Control-Request-Method header, or an OPTIONS request for a path with
+// no OPTIONS handler of its own. Any other OPTIONS request goes on to the
+// handler that was registered for it.
+func CORS(options CORSOptions) func(http.Handler) http.Handler {
+	return func(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
+		return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+			setCORSHeaders(w, r, options)
+
+			if r.Method == http.MethodOptions {
+				methods := routeMethods(r)
+				if isPreflight(r, methods) {
+					servePreflight(w, r, options, methods)
+					return
+				}
+			}
+			next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
+		})
+	}
+}
+
+// EnableCORS turns on CORS with DefaultCORSOptions for every route of the
+// router: responses carry the CORS headers, a preflight request is answered
+// with 204 and the methods the requested path serves, and a request with a
+// method the path does not serve gets a 405 with an Allow header.
+func (mx *Mux) EnableCORS() {
+	mx.EnableCORSWithOptions(DefaultCORSOptions())
+}
